# Robustness {#sec-robustness}

The pre-registration fixed the robustness rows before any confirmatory result was seen (PAP §8.2), and every row was run. @fig-robustness-rq1 and @fig-robustness-market place the RQ1 and the H5 and H5b rows beside the primary estimates; each row's full record is in Appendix D (@sec-app-robustness-tables).

{{< include _generated/figures/robustness-rq1.md >}}

{{< include _generated/figures/robustness-market.md >}}

## What the rows vary

Construction rows change how the exposure measure is built: the later OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r1 >}} weights (R1, look-ahead for H5 and H5b), wage-bill weights (R2), dropping rather than zero-assigning occupations without AEI usage (R3, D3), the API source for Design `A_pooled` (R4), the suppression bounds in place of the point measure (R10), employment-weighted task allocation (R11), standardised ranks (R12), the AIOE crosswalk (R14), the headquarters industry redistributed (R15), the r6 task-allocated basis (R16), the GPT-4 Eloundou β (R17), the majority crosswalk mode (R20), other indices in place of `z_delegation` (R21), strict real-time inputs (R32) and the employment-weighted NAICS-to-SIC crosswalk (R33). Sample rows change which industries or days enter: FF30 and FF48 granularity (R6), dropping Hardw, Softw and Chips (R7), excluding the large-cap rally year in Design A (R8), placebo event dates (R9) and dropping Softw (R13). The returns row uses equal-weighted industry returns (R5). Inference rows change the null scale or the statistic: non-overlapping windows (R18), the root mean square around the null value (R19), earlier-starting windows (R34), the studentised statistic (R35) and one-way occupation clustering (R38). RQ1 rows vary the behavioural hypotheses (R22 to R28, R31, R36 and R37), and the H6 rows vary the filing sample and the dictionary (R29, R30).

## Reporting rules

The rules are those of PAP §8.1, fixed in `{{< var pap.tag >}}` and set out in @sec-methods. Every row is reported, and the summary table of Appendix D (@sec-app-robustness-tables) sets each row's estimate beside the primary's. Only R13, a co-condition of the H5 and H5b claim, bears on a decision; no row, R21 included, carries error control across rows, and rows are not tallied. Market rows recompute the null scale s, the null value b̄ and the critical for their own exposure vector or sample over the same {{< var power.n_windows >}} pre-seal windows, with the t₂₁ rule and the D21 null. Every market robustness interval here, for H5, H5b and the H6 gap–return slope, is b̂ ± c·s with c the row's critical at {{< var design.alpha.h5_second >}} (R35 uses its own scale and t₂₁ critical); no row file prints the interval at the first Holm level, {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}. No row-level MDE is computed, so this section reports estimates, intervals and p and calls no market row not rejected, which would need the P14 form of @sec-markets.

## RQ1

H1 is {{< var rq1.h1.decision_text >}}: the null that β_e or β_w is zero is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h1 >}} (@sec-rq1). R24 r5 is the one robustness row under which the H1 p-value, {{< var rob.r24.r5.p_h1.p >}}, falls below that level with both coefficients negative (β_e = {{< var rob.r24.r5.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r24.r5.log_wage.estimate >}}); it changes no decision. The other rows that move the H1 coefficients furthest are R24 r4, where β_w changes sign to {{< var rob.r24.r4.log_wage.estimate >}}; R24 `r6_1p_api` (β_e = {{< var rob.r24.r6_1p_api.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r24.r6_1p_api.log_wage.estimate >}}); R26 with GWA fixed effects (β_e = {{< var rob.r26.gwa.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r26.gwa.log_wage.estimate >}}) and with DWA fixed effects (β_e = {{< var rob.r26.dwa.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r26.dwa.log_wage.estimate >}}); and R10 at the upper bound (β_e = {{< var rob.r10.h1_ub.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r10.h1_ub.log_wage.estimate >}}).

H2 is {{< var rq1.h2.decision_text >}}: the release-level co-condition fails. Its measured rise is one r2-to-r3 step followed by a fall, leaving out r2 reverses the sign of β ({{< var diag.h2.leave_out_release_r2.beta >}}), and the step coincides with a change of the classified-conversation base, so classifier or platform drift cannot be separated from behaviour (@sec-rq1). The rows that run the other way are R22 on the API source over r3 to r5 ({{< var rob.r22.api_r3_r5.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r22.api_r3_r5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r22.api_r3_r5.ci_hi >}}]) and R23 with `ai_autonomy_mean` ({{< var rob.r23.h2.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r23.h2.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r23.h2.ci_hi >}}]). In the primary's direction lie R22's all-releases series ({{< var rob.r22.all_r2_r6.estimate >}}), labelled confounded with the r6 suppression-regime change, R22's unbalanced panel ({{< var rob.r22.unbalanced.estimate >}}) and R36 with publication dates ({{< var rob.r36.h2.estimate >}}); R37, descriptive, gives a within-r6 change of {{< var rob.r37.h2.estimate >}}.

H3 is {{< var rq1.h3.decision_text >}}: the null that γ is zero is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h3 >}}. No generated file ranks its rows: R10 at the upper bound, {{< var rob.r10.h3_ub.estimate >}} (interval [{{< var rob.r10.h3_ub.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r10.h3_ub.ci_hi >}}]); R27, the continuous Consequence of Error, {{< var rob.r27.h3.estimate >}} pp per standard deviation; R31, with H1's covariates, {{< var rob.r31.error_cost.estimate >}}; and R38, {{< var rob.r38.h3.estimate >}} (p = {{< var rob.r38.h3.p >}}).

H4 is {{< var rq1.h4.decision_text >}} (@sec-rq1), and its rows are not ranked either. R25 tests the coefficients separately in a five-member Holm family: p = {{< var rob.r25.h4a.p >}} for b₁ and p = {{< var rob.r25.h4b.p >}} for b₂. R28 changes units and weights: US states (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.us_states.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.us_states.log_income.estimate >}}), r4 countries (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_aui.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_aui.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_aui.ci_hi >}}]; b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_income.estimate >}}), r5 countries (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.r5_countries.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.r5_countries.log_income.estimate >}}), usage weights (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.usage_weighted.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.usage_weighted.log_income.estimate >}}) and the IWA-level mix (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.iwa_mix.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.iwa_mix.log_income.estimate >}}).

## Market rows

H5 (b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5.b_pp2 >}} pp per standard deviation) is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}}, in the fixed wording of @sec-markets. The rows that move b̂ furthest are R7, dropping Hardw, Softw and Chips ({{< var rob.r07.h5.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r07.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r07.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r07.h5.p >}}); R12, standardised ranks ({{< var rq3.h5_r12.b >}}); and R5, equal-weighted returns ({{< var rob.r05.h5.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r05.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r05.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r05.h5.p >}}). H5b (b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5b.b_pp2 >}}) is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}; the rows that move it furthest are R12 ({{< var rq3.h5b_r12.b >}}), R7 ({{< var rob.r07.h5b.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r07.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r07.h5b.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r07.h5b.p >}}) and R6 at FF30 ({{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.p >}}).

Every H5 and H5b number carries the S1 caveat of @sec-data and @sec-markets: Design B's {{< var vintage.oews.primary >}} OEWS weights and O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.primary >}} links postdate the {{< var design.formation >}} formation date, so Design B is out of sample in AEI data only, not strictly real-time. R32, the strict real-time row ({{< var vintage.oews.r32 >}} weights), gives {{< var rob.r32.h5.estimate >}} for H5 (interval [{{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_hi >}}]) and {{< var rob.r32.h5b.estimate >}} for H5b (interval [{{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_hi >}}]); R1, labelled look-ahead, gives {{< var rob.r01.h5.estimate >}} and {{< var rob.r01.h5b.estimate >}}.

## H6

H6 is exploratory throughout (@sec-markets). Its divergence Spearman is ρ = {{< var h6.spearman.rho >}} (interval [{{< var h6.spearman.ci.lo >}}, {{< var h6.spearman.ci.hi >}}]). Two inputs are fixed at retrieval ({{< var h6.vintage.submissions_retrieved_utc >}}), not at the filing year: each filer's FF49 industry is its current SIC from the EDGAR submissions file, and the numerator uses the SEC full-text search's phrase matching on the retrieval date. The R29 parts whose intervals cover zero are the change in talk ({{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.ci_hi >}}]), the float-weighted filers ({{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.ci_hi >}}]) and the pre-formation filings ({{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.ci_hi >}}]). R30's narrow and broad dictionaries give {{< var rob.r30.h6_divergence.narrow.estimate >}} and {{< var rob.r30.h6_divergence.broad.estimate >}}. The exploratory gap–return slope is {{< var h6.gap_returns.b >}} pp per standard deviation of the gap in the primary and {{< var rob.r29.h6_gap_return.change_2019_2024.estimate >}} under the change in talk (interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_gap_return.change_2019_2024.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_gap_return.change_2019_2024.ci_hi >}}]); no MDE computed (exploratory).

## Where the rows are

Appendix D (@sec-app-robustness-tables) prints each row file unedited, the summary table, and the table of implementation choices where the PAP is silent, each with the §11 clarification it names. It also records the reproduction tolerance for the row files (PAP §11, C-80): a re-run reproduces every row file byte for byte, or a regenerated CSV has identical non-numeric cells and numeric cells within a fixed relative tolerance.
